title: Introduction to Beaujolais
description: Discover Burgundy's iconoclast — Beaujolais. Learn about Gamay, carbonic maceration, and the distinctive character of the ten Crus.
lessons.0.title: Beaujolais: Burgundy's Rebel
lessons.0.content.sections.0.heading: What Makes Beaujolais So Different?
lessons.0.content.sections.0.keyPoints.3: Style: fruit-forward, low tannin, best drunk young
lessons.0.content.sections.0.keyPoints.4: Culture: Beaujolais Nouveau Day (the third Thursday of November)
lessons.0.content.sections.1.heading: Past and Present of Gamay
lessons.0.content.sections.1.text: Gamay (full name Gamay Noir à Jus Blanc) is a natural cross of Pinot Noir and Gouais Blanc. In 1395 the Duke of Burgundy, Philippe le Hardi, banned Gamay from the Côte d'Or, calling it "vile" and confining it to Beaujolais. Ironically, that decree turned Beaujolais into Gamay's perfect home.
lessons.0.content.sections.1.keyPoints.0: Origin: a natural cross from Burgundy
lessons.0.content.sections.1.keyPoints.1: Character: high-yielding, early-ripening, well suited to poor soils
lessons.0.content.sections.1.keyPoints.2: Aromatics: red cherry, strawberry, banana, bubblegum
lessons.0.content.sections.1.keyPoints.3: Tannin: low; suited to early drinking
lessons.0.content.sections.1.keyPoints.4: Plantings worldwide: 90% in France, rare elsewhere
lessons.0.content.sections.2.heading: The Magic of Granite
lessons.0.content.sections.2.text: All ten Cru villages of northern Beaujolais sit on granite — completely different from the limestone of the Côte d'Or. Granite is poor, free-draining and rich in minerals: it limits yields and lifts quality.
lessons.0.content.sections.3.heading: Carbonic Maceration
lessons.0.content.sections.3.text: This is Beaujolais's signature technique. Whole, unbroken bunches go into a sealed vat that is then flooded with CO₂; the grapes ferment intracellularly under anaerobic conditions, extracting bright fruit and colour with very little tannin.
lessons.0.content.tips.0: 🍇 Gamay is at its best on granite, more ordinary on limestone
lessons.0.content.tips.1: 🍇 Carbonic maceration was invented in Beaujolais
lessons.0.content.tips.2: 🍇 Many Cru wines use traditional vinification and can age longer
lessons.0.content.tips.3: 🍇 Beaujolais Nouveau is only 25% of total production — don't be misled
lessons.0.content.summary: Gamay, granite and carbonic maceration give Beaujolais a style worlds apart from the Pinot Noir of the Côte d'Or — the clearest possible illustration of Burgundy's diversity.
lessons.1.title: The Ten Crus: An In-depth Look
lessons.1.slides.0.title: The Ten Crus: An In-depth Look
lessons.1.slides.0.subtitle: 20 minutes
lessons.1.slides.0.description: The heart of Beaujolais lies in its ten Crus, all on the granite slopes of the north. These villages produce complex, age-worthy wines that overturn the cliché of "simple Beaujolais Nouveau".

lessons.1.slides.2.title: Overview of the Ten Crus
lessons.1.slides.2.content: All ten Crus lie on granite slopes in northern Beaujolais, arranged from north to south, each with its own terroir and style.
lessons.1.slides.2.keyPoints.0: 🏔️ Location: all on the granite slopes of the north
lessons.1.slides.2.keyPoints.3: 🍷 Style: from elegantly perfumed to powerful and complex
lessons.1.slides.3.title: 👑 Moulin-à-Vent — King of Beaujolais
lessons.1.slides.3.content: Moulin-à-Vent is the most powerful and complex Cru. With age it is often mistaken for Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir.
lessons.1.slides.3.keyPoints.10: • With age, takes on a Pinot Noir-like character
lessons.1.slides.3.keyPoints.12: 🍽️ Food pairing: roast meats, game, mature cheese
lessons.1.slides.4.title: 🍒 Morgon — The Distinctive "Morgon Character"
lessons.1.slides.4.content: Morgon is the largest of the Crus (1,100 ha), famed for its distinctive "morgonner" character and the Côte de Py lieu-dit.
lessons.1.slides.4.keyPoints.1: 🪨 Soil: decomposed blue granite (Côte de Py)
lessons.1.slides.4.keyPoints.10: • Côte de Py is the very greatest plot in all Beaujolais
lessons.1.slides.4.keyPoints.12: 🍽️ Food pairing: beef stew, roast duck, wild mushrooms
lessons.1.slides.5.title: 🌸 Fleurie — Queen of Beaujolais
lessons.1.slides.5.content: With its elegant, perfumed style Fleurie is known as the "Queen of Beaujolais" — and is one of the most popular Crus.
lessons.1.slides.5.keyPoints.10: • The most perfumed of the Crus
lessons.1.slides.5.keyPoints.12: 🍽️ Food pairing: roast chicken, salmon, mild cheeses
lessons.1.slides.6.title: Three Northern Crus: Saint-Amour, Juliénas, Chénas
lessons.1.slides.6.content: The three northernmost Crus, each with its own personality.
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.3: • Light and elegant, drink within 2–5 years
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.8: • Red berries, peony floral notes, spice
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.10: • €12–30, with roast pork, ham, Chinese braised dishes
lessons.1.slides.7.title: Two Central Crus: Chiroubles, Régnié
lessons.1.slides.7.content: Both villages produce a lighter, more delicate style well suited to early drinking.
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.1: • 360 ha, the highest in altitude (400 m)
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.4: • Lightest in body, delicate and supple
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.6: • Pairs with charcuterie, light dishes, Japanese cuisine
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.9: • 400 ha, only promoted to Cru status in 1988
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.11: • Red berries, banana, fresh fruit aromatics
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.13: • Pairs with roast chicken, pizza, light dishes
lessons.1.slides.8.title: Two Southern Crus: Brouilly, Côte de Brouilly
lessons.1.slides.8.content: Two Crus around Mont Brouilly. Côte de Brouilly is unique in having volcanic soils.
lessons.1.slides.8.keyPoints.5: • €10–25, with grilled meats, hotpot, home cooking
lessons.1.slides.8.keyPoints.13: • Pairs with grilled meats, game, rich sauces
lessons.1.slides.8.keyPoints.14: • A more concentrated take on Brouilly
lessons.1.slides.9.title: How to Choose a Cru
lessons.1.slides.9.content: Choose a Cru that matches your palate and the occasion.
lessons.1.slides.10.title: 💡 Key Take-aways
lessons.1.slides.10.points.0: 🍷 Aged Moulin-à-Vent is often mistaken for Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir
lessons.1.slides.10.points.1: 🍷 Côte de Py in Morgon is the very greatest plot in all of Beaujolais
lessons.1.slides.10.points.2: 🍷 Fleurie is the most loved by women, with floral aromatics in spades
lessons.1.slides.10.points.3: 🍷 Côte de Brouilly is the only Cru on volcanic soils
lessons.1.slides.10.points.4: 🍷 Chénas is the smallest (285 ha) and the rarest
lessons.1.slides.10.points.6: 🍷 All ten Crus can age — they are not just for early drinking
lessons.1.slides.11.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.0.question: Which variety is the heart of Beaujolais, and what is its hallmark style?
A. Pinot Noir, with deep ageing potential
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.0.explanat: Gamay is the soul of Beaujolais, prized for lively red fruit and floral aromatics. The use of carbonic maceration — whole-bunch fermentation in CO₂ — produces the bright, juicy, easy-drinking style that defines Beaujolais.
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.1.question: When does Beaujolais Nouveau go on sale each year?
A. Early September, immediately after harvest
B. The third Thursday of November
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.1.explanat: Beaujolais Nouveau is released worldwide on the third Thursday of November as a "new wine season" marketing event — once one of the great wine-marketing successes. The hype has cooled, but it remains hugely popular in Japan and elsewhere.
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.2.question: Which of the following are among the most famous Beaujolais Crus? (multiple answers)
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.2.explanat: Moulin-à-Vent (the most powerful and ageable), Fleurie (the most floral and elegant) and Morgon (earthy, mineral, with real ageing potential) are all top Cru villages of Beaujolais. Chambertin is a Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir Grand Cru — not a Beaujolais village.
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.3.question: How does a Beaujolais Cru differ from generic Beaujolais?
A. They are exactly the same — only the name differs
B. The Cru Gamay is more concentrated, and some can age 5–10 years
C. Crus are all white wines
D. Crus use Pinot Noir rather than Gamay
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.3.explanat: Gamay from the ten Crus, on granite and under stricter rules of production, is far more complex than basic Beaujolais: deeper in colour, firmer in structure. Moulin-à-Vent in particular can age over ten years, taking on Pinot-like complexity.
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.4.question: What does carbonic maceration do for the style of Beaujolais?
A. Increases tannin and deepens colour
B. Produces a juicy, fruit-laden, low-tannin style
C. Speeds up ageing and maturation
lessons.1.slides.11.questions.4.explanat: Carbonic maceration (whole bunches undergoing intracellular fermentation in CO₂) limits tannin extraction and preserves vibrant fruit aromatics — strawberry, banana, elderflower — yielding Beaujolais's signature easy-drinking style, but also a wine not built for long ageing.
lessons.1.slides.12.title: Summary
lessons.1.slides.12.content: The ten Crus showcase the diversity Gamay can express on granite — from elegant Fleurie to powerful Moulin-à-Vent — proving that Beaujolais is far more than "Nouveau". Each village has its own personality and rewards exploration.
lessons.2.title: Tasting Beaujolais and Food Pairing
lessons.2.content.sections.0.heading: Key Points for Tasting Beaujolais
lessons.2.content.sections.0.keyPoints.0: Temperature: lightly chilled (12–14 °C); in summer down to 10 °C
lessons.2.content.sections.0.keyPoints.1: Glass: a larger red-wine glass to release the fruit aromatics
lessons.2.content.sections.0.keyPoints.2: Colour: violet-red when young, garnet with age
lessons.2.content.sections.0.keyPoints.3: Aromatics: red cherry, strawberry, banana, bubblegum, violet
lessons.2.content.sections.0.keyPoints.4: Palate: low tannin, medium body, fruit-rich and refreshing
lessons.2.content.sections.1.heading: How Different Styles Compare on the Palate
lessons.2.content.sections.2.heading: Suggested Food Pairings
lessons.2.content.sections.3.heading: The Golden Rules of Pairing Beaujolais
lessons.2.content.sections.4.heading: Serving Temperature Matters!
lessons.2.content.sections.4.text: The most common mistake is serving Beaujolais like a regular red at room temperature (18–20 °C) — which makes the wine feel slack and dull. Always serve it lightly chilled:
lessons.2.content.tips.0: 🍽️ Beaujolais is the perfect partner for Asian cuisine
lessons.2.content.tips.1: 🍽️ The ideal choice for picnics, barbecues and parties
lessons.2.content.tips.2: 🍽️ If you don't like heavy tannin, you'll fall in love with Beaujolais
lessons.2.content.tips.3: 🍽️ Morgon with red-braised pork is a marriage made in heaven
lessons.2.content.summary: With its low tannin, fruit and easy drinkability, Beaujolais is an all-rounder at the table. Just remember to serve it lightly chilled — and never miss the wonderful pairing it makes with Asian cuisine.
